_comment: GRAND over the Cajatambo / upper Pativilca crop, cut from the LIMA DEM (2881 x 2881 px, ~8.3 Mpx: -10.30..-11.10 lat, -77.60..-76.80 lon) and run unbiased at downsample_factor 1 / candidate_stride 1. Two reasons. It is where Lima's TAMBO sites are densest -- 17 of 40, and the largest of them. And it is the SAME GROUND as the south-east corner of the Ancash box, which reaches past the department border: the largest joint patch in the whole Ancash run reverse-geocodes to Gorgor, Cajatambo, Lima (ROADMAP 6.48). Both DEMs are SRTMGL1, so running it from the Lima side is a reproducibility check on the whole pipeline across two independently downloaded, differently aligned crops of the same terrain. Every criterion is copied unchanged from GRAND_lima_full.json except the sampling.
_comment_unbiased: 1 and 1. At 8.3 Mpx the estimator puts this at 2.04 GiB for the search plus 0.49 for the map, against ~8.5 GiB available, so neither the ~30% area loss from downsampling nor the fragmentation penalty from striding applies -- the latter measured at 291x for TAMBO on the Huaylas crop (ROADMAP 6.49). These areas are real rather than lower bounds, which is exactly what makes them comparable with the Huaylas crop and not with the department runs.
_comment_rfi: none, as for Ancash and for the same reason. There IS a 'lima' RFI preset, but using it here would make Lima the only one of the three department runs with settlement exclusion of its own kind -- Arequipa uses its preset, Ancash uses none. Holding it at none keeps Lima comparable to Ancash, and the difference against Arequipa is stated there: its five circles cover ~3,500 km2 of a ~120,000 km2 box, so roughly 2.9%.
_comment_origin: Deliberately null: read from the DEM's own ModelTiepointTag. The crop configs carry the crop's corner, which is not this file's.
